newsitem.title: PANAMA: Most Panamanians find government corrupt, poll.
newsitem.headline: Most Panamanians find government corrupt, poll.

text.p: Most Panamanians find the government of President Ernesto Perez Balladares corrupt and do not favour his re-election, according to a poll published on Sunday in the daily newspaper La Prensa.
The poll surveyed 1,226 Panamanians over age 18 and had a margin of error of 3 percentage points. Details of when the survey took place were not available.
According to those polled, 82 percent of Panamanians said Perez Balladares' government was corrupt, and 72 percent were not in favour of his re-election.

Although the Constitution allows only one, five-year presidential term, a commission of the ruling Democratic Revolutionary Party (PRD) was studying changing the limit in time for the May 1999 elections.

According to those polled, the so-called "narco-checks" scandal hurt the Perez Balladares administration the most. The political scandal began last May when an audit of Panama's ruling party turned up a $51,000 contribution made by jailed Colombian drug lord Jose Castrillon Henao to Perez Balladares' 1994 campaign.

And 64 percent of Panamanians said the process to privatise state enterprises was corrupt. Panama's Foreign Minister, Ricardo Arias, recently dismissed complaints from U.S. Ambassador to Panama William Hughes that Panama's privatisation processes have not been transparent.
Hughes said in a letter to Commerce Minister Raul Arango that several U.S. senators have received complaints from American companies alleging unfair treatment in Panama.
